tools.name: upload_image
tools.description: Upload an image to BasePic and get links: page_url (short link to share), image_url (direct image) and download_url. Give either a public "url" (an image, or a post on X/Instagram/Facebook) or "image_base64". Returns an id for edit_image and a delete_key. Images up to 50 MB. The image is private: on

tools.name: edit_image
tools.description: Edit an uploaded image: rotate, flip, crop (pixels or aspect ratio), resize (width/height, percent, megapixels), grayscale (black & white), sepia, brightness, contrast, warm, cool, invert, blur, sharpen — applied in order. Optionally change the format (jpeg/png/webp) or make the file at most max_kb

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: Get the links and details (size, dimensions, type) of an image on BasePic by its id.

tools.name: delete_image
tools.description: Delete an image from BasePic. Needs the delete_key returned when it was uploaded or created by edit_image. Its links stop working.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upload_image · Private data: upload_image, edit_image · Public sink: upload_image · Destructive: upload_image, edit_image, delete_image.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upload_image · Private data: upload_image, edit_image · Public sink: upload_image · Destructive: upload_image, edit_image, delete_image

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "upload_image" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
